construction_markdown:
No new code above dimension 1040 is claimed. The numerical construction fields report the independently certified campaign anchor used for every comparison.

Fix `F=F_2[α]/(α^16+α^5+α^3+α^2+1)`, `A=span_F2{1,α,…,α^14}`, and `Y=F_2^15`. Write `z=Σ_(i=0)^15 z_i α^i` and define `H(z)_y=z_0+Σ_(i=1)^15 z_i y_i`. The anchor is

`C_0={ (H(f(a))_y)_(a,y) : f∈F[X], deg f≤64 }`.

Both `A` and `Y` have size 32768, so the length is exactly `2^30`. A basis consists of the 1040 words obtained from `f=α^iX^j`, with `0≤i≤15` and `0≤j≤64`. Since `a↦a^j` has Boolean degree at most the binary popcount of `j`, and every `j≤64` has popcount at most 6, `C_0⊆RM(7,30)` in the natural `(a,y)` coordinates.

The new contribution is a finite Reed–Muller extension obstruction: `C_0` cannot acquire even one missing affine `a`-coordinate, and any target-safe augmentation by words from `RM(2,30)` can add at most 105 dimensions and must be a genuinely coupled graph between pure `y`-quadratics and non-RS blockwise-affine functions. No such nonzero safe graph was constructed.

Then `C(P)+λ` has exact weight `(32768-128)16384=534773760<D`. distance_audit: The immutable requirement is `D=(1/2-2^-10)2^30=2^29-2^20=535822336`; its signed-sum cap is `2^30-2D=2^21`.

For nonconstant `f` of degree at most 64, let `N_b(f)=|{a∈A:f(a)=b}|`. The affine-inner spectrum gives `wt(C(f))=2^14(32768-N_0(f)+N_1(f))`. Since `N_0(f)≤64`, every nonzero word has weight at least `D`. A degree-64 polynomial with 64 roots, scaled to avoid value 1 at every nonroot, attains `D`.
For the affine-row witness, `P^{-1}(0)∩A=U` and `P^{-1}(1)∩A=a_0+U`. These 128 blocks cancel; every other block is balanced. Its exact weight is `2^29-2^21=534773760=D-2^20`.
Fixed-inner additive maximality supplies weight at most `2^14(32768-65)=535805952=D-16384` for every strict additive outer extension under the unchanged affine encoder.
A nonzero pure `y`-quadratic has polar rank `2h≤14`. After adding a suitable affine `y`-word already in `C_0`, its repeated-block weight is `2^29-2^(29-h)≤2^29-2^22=532676608<D`.
For an inner subcode of `RM(r,14)`, `r≤4`, every weight is divisible by 8. Thus distance at least 8188 would imply distance at least 8192, but `g_16(8192)=16385>16384`.

For the degree-69 trace gateway, the generic signed-sum bound is `68·2^15=2228224`, exceeding the permitted `64·2^15=2097152` by 131072; equivalently, the generic distance certificate misses `D` by 65536.
explicitness_audit: The field polynomial, evaluation space, coordinate ordering, row ordering, and every generator entry of `C_0` are symbolic and deterministic.
The full generator is streamed without random sampling, puncturing, padding, lookup tables, or a conditional selector.
Given `λ`, Gaussian elimination deterministically chooses `U≤ker λ` and `a_0`; multiplying the 64 displayed linear factors constructs the bad extension witness in polynomial time.
The ordinary-RS and trace-orbit scans use deterministic cyclotomic-orbit enumeration and exact integer arithmetic in time polynomial in `n`; they are proof audits, not hidden construction searches.
No generator is asserted for a quadratic augmentation or for the conditional degree-69, inner-code, or AG gateways.
The workspace was read-only, so this note could not be added under `proofs/`, and the data validator and dashboard build were not run.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Order `A` and `Y` by their 15-bit coefficient vectors. Index rows lexicographically by `(j,i)` with `0≤j≤64` and `0≤i≤15`. At column `(a,y)`, compute `z=α^i a^j` modulo `α^16+α^5+α^3+α^2+1`, write `z=Σz_sα^s`, and output `z_0+Σ_(s=1)^15 z_s y_s`. These are exactly the entries of `C(α^iX^j)`.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: At most `1040·n·[64(256 AND + 300 XOR)+30]` elementary bit operations, plus exactly `1040n` output writes; hence `O(n)` for the fixed parameters and certainly `n^{O(1)}`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Naive multiplication of two degree-below-16 binary polynomials followed by reduction modulo the fixed pentanomial uses at most 256 coefficient products and fewer than 300 XORs. Computing `a^j` naively needs at most 63 multiplications, multiplication by `α^i` needs one more, and evaluating `H` needs at most 30 bit operations. There are exactly `1040n` entries. Lexicographic counters and degree-16 field registers suffice, so the matrix can be streamed with polynomial time and constant-size arithmetic state apart from the output.

proof_markdown:
### 1. Certified Reed–Muller anchor

The stated quotient polynomial is irreducible by the accepted Rabin certificate, so `F` has 65536 elements. The maps `f↦(f(a))_(a∈A)` and `H` are binary-linear. The coordinate set has size `|A||Y|=32768^2=2^30`.

The message space has dimension `65·16=1040`. If its image is zero, injectivity of `H` makes `f` vanish at every point of `A`. Since `deg f≤64<32768`, this forces `f=0`; hence the dimension is exactly 1040.

For nonconstant `f`, both `f` and `f-1` have at most 64 roots. The block spectrum of `H` is weight 0 at symbol 0, weight 32768 at symbol 1, and weight 16384 otherwise. Therefore

`wt(C(f))=2^14(32768-N_0(f)+N_1(f))≥2^14(32768-64)=D`.

The constant cases are immediate. Exact equality follows by taking a polynomial with 64 prescribed roots and scaling it so none of its 32704 nonroot values is 1; at most 32704 of the 65535 nonzero scales are forbidden.

Finally, `a^j=∏_(s:j_s=1)a^(2^s)` is a product of `popcount(j)` binary-linear Frobenius maps. Thus its coordinate functions have Boolean degree at most `popcount(j)≤6`, and multiplication by a `y` variable in `H` raises degree by at most one. Hence `C_0⊆RM(7,30)`.

### 2. Exact affine-row obstruction

Let `λ:A→F_2` be nonzero linear. Choose a 6-dimensional `U≤ker λ` and `a_0∈A` with `λ(a_0)=1`. Its subspace polynomial

`L_U(X)=∏_(u∈U)(X-u)`

is additive and has kernel exactly `U`. Since `a_0∉U`, define `P(X)=L_U(X)/L_U(a_0)`. It has degree 64, so `C(P)∈C_0`. Additivity gives

`P(a)=0 iff a∈U`, and `P(a)=1 iff a∈a_0+U`.

On `U`, both `H(P(a))` and `λ(a)` vanish. On `a_0+U`, they are both the constant-one block and cancel. Outside those two fibers, `P(a)∉{0,1}`, so `H(P(a))+λ(a)` is balanced. Consequently

`wt(C(P)+λ)=(32768-128)16384=534773760<D`.

Thus no target-safe supercode of `C_0` contains a nonconstant affine function of `a`, and none contains natural `RM(1,30)`.

For completeness, `C_0∩RM(1,30)` is exactly the 16-dimensional space of affine functions of `y`. Indeed, if `C(f)` is globally affine, then after subtracting a constant field symbol its outer value is a polynomial `p(a)` taking only values 0 and 1. The degree-at-most-128 polynomial `p(p-1)` vanishes at all 32768 points of `A`, hence is identically zero; the integral-domain property forces `p` to be constant.

### 3. Quadratic graph ceiling

Every `q∈RM(2,30)` has a unique decomposition

`q(a,y)=Q_y(y)+H(g_q(a))_y`,

where `Q_y` is a squarefree homogeneous quadratic in the 15 variables `y`, the constant coordinate of `g_q` has degree at most 2 in `a`, and its other 15 coordinates have degree at most 1. The first space has dimension `C(15,2)=105`; the blockwise-affine space has dimension `(1+15+105)+15(1+15)=361`.

Let `W≤RM(2,30)` and suppose `C_0+W` meets the target. Project `W` onto `Q_y`. If `q` lies in the kernel, then `q=H(g_q)`. Unless `g_q` belongs to the outer RS evaluation space `R`, this creates a strict binary-additive outer extension under the unchanged encoder. Fixed-inner additive maximality supplies a word of weight at most 535805952, a contradiction. Hence

`ker(π|W)=W∩C_0`,

so `W/(W∩C_0)` injects into a 105-dimensional space and

`dim(C_0+W)≤1040+105=1145`.

There is also no pure quadratic escape. If `g_q∈R`, adding an anchor word leaves `Q_y` alone. A nonzero quadratic in 15 variables has polar rank `2h` with `1≤h≤7`; some affine shift has Walsh magnitude `2^(15-h)`. Every affine `y`-shift is already in `C_0`, so repeating this shift over all 32768 outer blocks produces weight

`2^29-2^(29-h)≤2^29-2^22<D`.

Thus projection of the new quotient onto `g_q mod R` is injective as well. Every possible augmentation is therefore a genuinely coupled graph; the argument does not assert that any nonzero graph is safe.

### 4. Low-degree inner RM obstruction

Let `B≤RM(r,14)` with `r≤4` and `d(B)≥8188`. Ax divisibility makes every word weight divisible by `2^floor(13/r)`, hence by 8. Therefore `d(B)≥8192`. If `dim B≥16`, Griesmer gives

`16384≥Σ_(i=0)^15 ceil(8192/2^i)=16385`,

a contradiction. Thus `dim B≤15`. In particular, neither conditional length-16384 inner gateway of dimension 16 or 17 can be realized inside order at most 4.

The exceptional-line dimension-1041 flag is similarly impossible in `RM(3,14)`. Divisibility by 16 raises every top-shell weight from 8184 to at least 8192. Its distinguished word is either at least 8192, immediately contradicting Griesmer, or has weight 8176. In the latter case, residualizing it gives `[8208,16,≥4104]_2`, whereas `g_16(4104)=8218>8208`.

### 5. Trace-layer finite optimization

Exact cyclotomic-orbit enumeration gives

`dim(C_69∩RM(r,30))=(31,211,571,871,1021,1051)` for `r=1,…,6`.

Thus RM order at most 5 cannot improve dimension 1040 within the degree-69 trace architecture. Order 6 reaches the full dimension 1051 family, but generic Weil gives only `|S|≤68·2^15`; the target requires `64·2^15`.

The upstream codimension-10 certificate is all-or-nothing: because the degree-65 anchor has dimension 991, any top-layer subspace large enough to beat 1040 has dimension at least 50, and such a safe subspace exists only if the entire 60-dimensional `(x^67,x^69)` layer is safe. Hence dimensions 1041 through 1050 are not independent trace checkpoints.

One mixed phase is rigorously safe. In characteristic two,

`Tr((x^2+x)^35)=Tr(x^69+x^67+x^37+x^19+x^17+x^9)`.

The map `x↦x^2+x` is two-to-one onto the trace-zero hyperplane, so its character sum equals `S(x^35)+S(x^35+x)`. Since `x↦x^5` permutes `F_(2^30)`, the first term reduces to degree 7. Weil therefore gives

`|S|≤6·2^15+34·2^15=40·2^15`.

This controls only that phase, not all its lower-degree cosets, so it is not a code extension.

### 6. Conclusion

The finite audit found no admissible `k>1040` construction. It proves three reusable exclusions: natural `RM(1,30)` cannot be adjoined to the accepted anchor; quadratic augmentation of that anchor is a coupled graph problem with added dimension at most 105; and all length-16384 RM inner subcodes of order at most 4 are too small for the surviving concatenation gateways. These are architecture-specific statements, not a global upper bound on binary codes.

theorem_statement: Let `C_0` be the explicit dimension-1040 RS–affine subcode of natural `RM(7,30)`. First, adjoining any nonconstant natural affine function of the 15 outer variables produces an explicit word of weight `2^29-2^21<D`; hence no target-safe supercode of `C_0` contains natural `RM(1,30)`. Second, if `W≤RM(2,30)` and `C_0+W` is target-safe, then `W/(W∩C_0)` injects into the 105-dimensional pure-`y` quadratic space, so `dim(C_0+W)≤1145`, with every surviving direction necessarily coupled. Third, every length-16384 subcode of `RM(r,14)`, `r≤4`, with distance at least 8188 has dimension at most 15. No new code above dimension 1040 is certified.
